description: The authors publish a Python 3.8 notebook that fills data gaps for the Chinese product, building and infrastructure material-stock collection. Native metadata names pandas 1.3.4, numpy 1.18.5, statsmodels 0.13.2, sklearn 1.0.2 and scipy 1.7.3; one notebook descriptor is listed. The parent collection identifies material-stock estimates for 337 prefecture-level cities from 1978 to 2020. The primary publication abstract confirms official-statistics collation and gap-filling methods. The software prepares the related, separately catalogued infrastructure-stock data. Figshare provides public free access under CC0. Coverage is the source workflow for China, not evidence of independent validation in other countries. The collection describes 43 product/infrastructure types while the publication abstract describes 10 types; classification levels are not reconciled here. No specific use from the controlled simulation-use vocabulary is established. A limitation is that the notebook was not read or executed, so gap-filling algorithms, accuracy, required input schemas and completeness remain unverified.
